_comment: Reference language. Every key must exist here; other languages may omit keys and fall back to this file. Keys prefixed 'Log' are written to the Emby log and are deliberately never translated - they must not appear in any other language file.
EditorDescription: Routes outbound HTTP(S) traffic initiated by the Emby core (metadata providers, remote images, subtitle downloads) through a proxy. Everything goes through it unless you bypass private networks or list exceptions below.
DescEnableProxy: When disabled, the Emby core connects directly - including when HTTP_PROXY or HTTPS_PROXY is set in the environment. While this plugin is installed it decides where that traffic goes, whether it is switched on or not.
DescScheme: Only used when the proxy address does not carry a scheme of its own.
DescProxyAddress: Either host:port (for example 192.168.1.10:8080) or a full URL (for example socks5://192.168.1.10:1080). Put credentials in the fields below - .NET ignores credentials embedded in the URL for SOCKS5.
DescUsername: Optional. Takes precedence over credentials embedded in the URL.
DescIgnoreCert: Required for HTTPS proxies using a self-signed certificate. Only takes effect while the proxy is enabled and configured, but then it applies to every outbound connection the Emby core makes - the proxy itself, the destinations tunnelled through it, and the destinations that go out directly because they are on the bypass list.
DescBypassPrivate: OFF (default): everything goes through the proxy, including private networks. ON: private networks (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x), link-local, IPv6 ULA and *.local are contacted directly instead. Switch this on if the server also talks to its own LAN - other Emby servers, DLNA endpoints, a local metadata cache - and you do not want that traffic crossing the proxy or dying with it. The server's own loopback address is never proxied either way.
DescBypassList: Additional entries, one per line. Accepts CIDR (10.0.0.0/8), a single IP, a hostname, or a wildcard (*.example.com). No DNS resolution is performed - hostnames are matched literally. Entries here are additional to whatever the switch above covers, and they apply even when it is off. Emby's licensing servers are not bypassed by default - add them here if you want them contacted directly.
PatchActive: Active - Emby core traffic passes through this plugin.
PatchDegraded: Active, but the proxy could not be attached to at least one HTTP handler: {0} Requests on that handler are refused rather than sent unproxied, so nothing escapes - but they do not reach the proxy either, and they will keep failing. Restarting the server usually clears this.
PatchInactive: NOT active - {0} No traffic is being redirected.
DisabledText: The proxy is switched off; Emby connects directly.
UnreachableSuffix: Requests that would use the proxy are failing.
ProbeDisabled: The proxy is switched off; Emby connects directly.
ProbeFailed: The check could not be run: {0}
ProbeTcpOnlyOk: {0} accepts connections. An HTTP proxy reveals nothing further until it is given a request to forward, so this confirms it is reachable, not that it forwards.
ProbeNotSocks5: {0}:{1} accepts connections but does not answer as a SOCKS5 proxy.
ProbeSocks5Silent: {0}:{1} accepts connections but never answers the SOCKS5 greeting. Check that this port really speaks SOCKS5 - an HTTP proxy waits for a request instead of replying, and looks exactly like this.
ProbeSocks5NoMethod: The SOCKS5 proxy rejected every authentication method offered.
ProbeSocks5Method: The SOCKS5 proxy selected authentication method {0}, which this plugin cannot perform.
ProbeSocks5Truncated: The SOCKS5 proxy closed the connection during authentication.
ProbeSocks5CredentialTooLong: Username or password is longer than the 255 bytes SOCKS5 allows.
ProbeSocks5Ok: {0} answers as a SOCKS5 proxy and requires no authentication.
ProbeSocks5AuthOk: {0} answers as a SOCKS5 proxy and accepted the credentials.
ProbeSocks5AuthRejected: The SOCKS5 proxy rejected the credentials for user '{0}'.
ProbeSocks5AuthIgnored: The proxy requires no authentication, so the username and password are not being used. Anything relying on them is not happening.
LogReasonBypassed: destination is on the bypass list
LogReasonNotAttached: the proxy could not be attached to this HTTP handler
ErrInvalidUrl: Proxy address is not a valid URL: {0}
ErrUnsupportedScheme: Unsupported proxy scheme '{0}'. Supported schemes are http, https and socks5.
ErrNeedPort: Proxy address needs a port, for example 192.168.1.10:8080 or socks5://192.168.1.10:1080
ErrPortNotNumber: The text after the last colon in the proxy address is not a port number. Write it as host:port, for example 192.168.1.10:8080
ErrUserInfoNeedsScheme: The proxy address carries credentials but no scheme. Write it as http://user:password@192.168.1.10:8080, or leave the credentials out of the address and use the username and password fields.
ErrInvalidHost: Proxy address contains an invalid host: {0}
ErrNeedExplicitPort: Proxy address needs an explicit port.
ErrPrefixFamily: Prefix length does not match the address family: {0}
